# ghrelease

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/internal/ghrelease"
```

Package ghrelease talks to the GitHub Releases API and decides which asset of a release belongs on this machine.

It exists because the installer and the self\-updater each grew their own copy of the same three things: the API calls, the download, and the rules for reading a platform out of an asset name. The copies drifted — one of them excluded every arm64 asset, the other scored only amd64 — so a machine could install the wrong architecture in two different ways.

## func [ArchOf](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/asset.go#L44>)

```go
func ArchOf(name string) string
```

ArchOf reports the GOARCH an asset name claims, or "" when it names none.

<a name="ArchScore"></a>
## func [ArchScore](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/asset.go#L61>)

```go
func ArchScore(name, goarch string) (int, bool)
```

ArchScore rates how well an asset's architecture fits goarch. The second result is false when the asset cannot run on this machine at all.

An asset that names no architecture fits by default: a release with a single build is the common case, and refusing it would leave nothing to install.

<a name="Excluded"></a>
## func [Excluded](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/asset.go#L20>)

```go
func Excluded(name string) bool
```

Excluded reports whether an asset should never be installed, whatever the machine. Architecture is deliberately not part of this: the right answer there depends on where apptide is running, so it is scored, not excluded.

<a name="ScoreBinary"></a>
## func [ScoreBinary](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/asset.go#L92>)

```go
func ScoreBinary(name, goarch string) int
```

ScoreBinary rates an asset that is expected to be a ready\-to\-run executable, as opposed to an archive to unpack. Returns 0 for assets to skip.

This is what self\-update wants: apptide publishes bare .exe files, and an archive would have to be unpacked before it could replace the binary.

<a name="VerifySHA256"></a>

```go
func VerifySHA256(path, want string) error
```

VerifySHA256 checks a downloaded file against an expected digest. A "sha256:" prefix is accepted so a config can name the algorithm it is using.

<a name="NewClient"></a>
### func [NewClient](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/ghrelease.go#L57>)

```go
func NewClient(token string) *Client
```

NewClient returns a client that sends token as a bearer credential when one is given. An empty token means unauthenticated, which GitHub rate\-limits to 60 requests an hour per address.

<a name="Client.ChecksumFor"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ChecksumFor](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/ghrelease.go#L324>)

```go
func (c *Client) ChecksumFor(ctx context.Context, assets []Asset, name string) (string, bool)
```

ChecksumFor downloads the release's checksum file and returns the digest recorded for asset. Missing checksums are not an error: most repositories publish none, and refusing to install from those would make the github source useless.

<a name="Client.Newest"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Newest](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/ghrelease.go#L116>)

```go
func (c *Client) Newest(ctx context.Context, repo string) (*Release, error)
```

Newest returns the most recent published release, pre\-release or not.

The "latest release" endpoint deliberately excludes pre\-releases, so a repository that only publishes those resolves to nothing at all.

<a name="Client.TagFuzzy"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [TagFuzzy](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/ghrelease.go#L86>)

```go
func (c *Client) TagFuzzy(ctx context.Context, repo, tag string) (*Release, error)
```

TagFuzzy returns the release for tag, retrying with the "v" prefix toggled. Repositories disagree on whether tags carry it, and a config should not have to know which convention a project picked.

<a name="NotFoundError"></a>
## type [NotFoundError](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/apptide/blob/main/internal/ghrelease/ghrelease.go#L67>)

NotFoundError reports a release or repository the API does not have. It is distinguished from other failures so a caller can retry a different tag without swallowing a rate limit as "not found".

